sample_unit: error-inserted radiology report variants (from 256 original reports)

links.outcome: LLM detection of inserted clinically consequential errors in radiology reports
links.effect: Physiologically impossible errors (E2) detected in 46.2% (CT) and 33.7% (MRI) for GPT-4.1 versus 32.7% and 25.0% for Llama 3.3; overall E2 success for GPT-4.1 was 16.3% CT, 8.7% MRI, 12.5% X-ray.
links.quote: Physiologically impossible errors (E2) showed the lowest performance: 46.2% (CT) and 33.7% (MRI) for GPT-4.1, compared with 32.7% and 25.0% for Llama 3.3, respectively.

links.outcome: LLM robustness to erroneous or implausible input content in radiology reports
links.effect: Error detection was type-dependent; GPT-4.1 detected mislabeling (E1) in 49.0% and Llama 3.3 in 33.7% for MRI, while E4 detection reached 85.4% for GPT-4.1 in X-ray.
links.quote: Mislabeling errors (E1) were detected in 49.0% by GPT‑4.1 and 33.7% by Llama 3.3 for MRI.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs for automated quality assurance/error detection of radiology reports

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the capability of GPT-4.1 and Llama 3.3 70B in detecting and categorizing injected errors in radiology reports in a zero-shot setting without testing specific deployment safeguards.
